newsitem.title: INDIA: India's IDBI sees business spurt 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: India's IDBI sees business spurt 20 pct.

text.p: The Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) expects to post a 20 percent growth in operations in 1997/98 (April-March), fuelled by better liquidity and an expected revival in credit demand, its chairman said.
"The outlook for the bank during the current year is expected to be good," IDBI chairman S.H.Khan told reporters.
IDBI is India's leading term lending bank.
Khan said the general investment climate this year was better because of improved liquidity conditions that had pulled down interest rates.
As India heads into what meteorologists have forecast will be its tenth successful monsoon in a row, IDBI sees demand for credit rising.
"With the expected good monsoon for the tenth successive year, demand (for credit) is expected to revive," he said.
Steps in the latest federal budget to promote industry, coupled with policy measures relating to power and telecommunication projects, will stimulate corporate investment, Khan said.

IDBI said its sanctions during 1996/97 fell to 170.49 billion rupees from 177.96 billion in the previous year but disbursements rose 6.9 percent to 114.34 billion rupees from 106.93 billion rupees in the previous year.
"The marginal decline in sanctions in 1996/97 was largely due to decline in operations under non-project loans and capital market products," Khan said.
Sanctions of foreign currency loans, at 25.82 billion rupees, registered a sharp 66.6 percent rise during the year, while disbursements at 17.85 billion rupees rose 16.5 percent.
The rise in disbursements was supported by a sharp 54.7 percent rise in project loan disbursements, Khan said.
"It is indicative of the progress in implementation of projects sanctioned in previous years despite the subdued conditions in the capital market," the chairman said.
IDBI's net worth rose by 13.9 percent to 72.13 billion rupees by the end of March 1997, a bank statement said.
IDBI's profit margin rose to 3.69 percent during 1996/97 compared to 3.66 percent in 1995/96, Khan said. Return on average net worth for the year was 16.86 percent against 19.69 percent.
IDBI's debt to equity ratio at end March 1997 was 5.2 to one compared to 5.4 to one at end March 1996.
The bank's earnings per share for 1997/98 were 16.76 rupees compared to 15.76 in 1995/96. The book value per share at end March 1997 stood at 107.17 rupees compared to 94.12 rupees.
But IDBI's non-performing assets (bad loans) rose to 10.3 percent from 9.4 percent, Khan said.
Profit after tax for 1996/97 was 11.44 billion rupees compared to 10.07 billion in the previous year.
